title: Microsoft Edge: upgraded Copilot new tab page, off by default
summary: Hold: the cost rating says indirect costs only, but the briefing also identifies an add-on licence cost for users who are not already licensed. The documented controls and rollout details are supported; the cost rating and rationale need to reflect that licensing dependency.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: MC1440972 says users must have a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence to access the experience.
claims.quote: To access this experience, users must have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The policy reference says users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence might see limited relevance in prompt-card content.
claims.quote: Users who do not have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license might experience limited relevance in Copilot prompt card content.

claims.claim: The licensing model is add-on, referring to the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence named in the notice.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on plan with specific licensing prerequisites.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/microsoft-365-copilot to sources to support the add-on classification.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate price or meter for the new tab page itself is published in the researched Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot new tab page" "price" "meter". Read the configure page, both policy references, Copilot service description and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/pay-as-you-go-meters; none names a separate new-tab-page price or meter.

claims.claim: The configure page's prerequisites name no licence.
claims.quote: Prerequisites: Before setting up the configuration policy, ensure you have a Microsoft Entra group set up in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center that includes the target users.

claims.claim: Access to browser context is a separate setting in the management service's Copilot tab.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Edge management service, select the Copilot tab, then use each dropdown to select Enabled or Disabled ... Access to browser context: Allows Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to use a user’s browser context

claims.claim: Copilot icon in the toolbar is a separate management service Copilot setting.
claims.quote: Copilot icon in the toolbar: Shows the Copilot icon in the Microsoft Edge for Business toolbar.

claims.claim: Copilot search box is separately listed as a management service Copilot setting.
claims.quote: Copilot search box: Shows a search box on the new tab page where users can chat with Copilot and search with Bing Autosuggest.

claims.claim: AI-generated text and editing is a separate management service Copilot setting.
claims.quote: AI-generated text and editing: Provides AI-generated text creation and editing for eligible text fields.

claims.claim: The interaction between the separate Copilot search box and Copilot new tab page settings is not described in the cited Learn pages.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot search box" "Copilot new tab page" settings interaction. Read Configuring Copilot Features, Configure the Copilot new tab page and CopilotNewTabPageEnabled; they list the settings but do not explain their interaction.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions: work cards
claims.claim: The researched documentation describes Cards off as a user setting, not a separately documented admin work-card switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot new tab page" "cards" "policy" disable. Read the configure FAQ, supported-policy list, CopilotNewTabPageEnabled and ConfigureNTPFeedTabVisibility; the FAQ documents user Cards settings, not a separate admin Cards switch.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The low cost rating and indirect-cost-only rationale agree with the page's identified licence dependency.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; "the known cost is admin time and communications"; "For tenants without licences for the target users, the cost is the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence Microsoft's notice names"
claims.fix: Set cost to medium. Replace the cost rationale with: "Medium. Microsoft's notice says target users need a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, so enabling for users who are not already licensed can require add-on licences. For already licensed users, rollout adds administrator time and communications."

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control that the governance checklist asks administrators to check or adjust has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: "Check the new tab page policies you already set (quick links, app launcher, background types)"; "Review the other Copilot settings ... and adjust each one"; the table contains only availability and feed visibility.
claims.fix: The Before rollout step about quick links, app launcher and background types, and the At rollout step about adjusting other recommended Copilot settings, name controls without table rows. Remove these two checklist bullets; retain the existing explanatory prose.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends verifying that affected users have a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence before enabling.
claims.quote: If your organization plans to enable the experience, we recommend that you: ... Verify that affected users have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends evaluating work-card exposure of files and calendar events and reviewing applicable AI governance and compliance requirements.
claims.quote: Evaluate the effect of surfacing organizational files and calendar events through work cards. Review applicable AI governance and compliance requirements before enabling the experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends notifying affected users.
claims.quote: Notify affected users about the updated new tab page.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating user guidance, training and support documentation.
claims.quote: Update relevant user guidance, training, and support documentation.
